When any subverse reaches a certain size then elections can be called to bring in new mods or replace old ones. Any account with a certain amount of karma in that subverse gets a vote. This should prevent many of the abuses currently being committed on reddit. What does everyone think?

I think we are pretty far from needing this, but it seems like a great way to counterbalance mods on a powertrip. May I suggest a separate subverse that would be dedicated to subverse elections or something like that? Having the vote within the subverse may not be a good idea since a power hungry mod could delete the link. Or else it would need to be a site admin type function, but at the moment, we only have one and he is working overtime.
Creating separate subverses is something people would be able to do, I would suggest that making election posts unbannable is a better method. Either way it probably won't be added immediately.

I agree there should be a mechanism in place to address any concerns about abusive mods. Who watches the watchers? We do. The only catch is whatever we choose to do will require admin involvement (at least currently) to replace the mods. Perhaps a gauge within each subverse to express moderator confidence by the subscribers? Voting could be governed by a minimum SCP and/or CCP score within that subbverse and having an account age of at least one month.

I would suggest that should the disapproval rating exceed a certain percentage, the subverse then be flagged for review. The rest of the election process could move forward from there.

Just my thoughts on the topic, I may be missing some fatal flaw somewhere. Feel free to point it out.

The idea of waiting for a mod disapproval is an interest one that should work and is a nice one. It is somewhat funny to think about if this was applied to US congress, their disaproval is high but no one wants to vote for a different person. So if we applied this to congress I would imagine that we would have constant elections where we re elect the same congressmen repeatedly. The idea of having an election counter might be better than a disapproval counter although either way I like the idea.
It works both ways though, if a moderator confidence score remains high for a specified length of time, there should be a nifty badge earned by the mod team. ;)

I think that the sidebar needs to be changeable only by community voat, not by a mod's will alone, AND that the mods must adhere to it. There must also be a history of changes.

The worst thing about reddit was that the communities built themselves and then the mods came in and took ownership telling people that "if they don't like it they should start their own sub, with cocaine and hookers".
Was it possible to get the cocaine and hookers without starting a sub? Otherwise it is all too much work.

What do you guys think about this manifesto for Russia written by the anarcho-libertarian founder of VK and Telegram?

Just because I'm no fan of reading filler, here's the list:

  1. Rid society of the burden of obsolete laws, licenses and restrictions that spawn corruption. The world is evolving too fast for regulators to adequately respond to its changes in the 21st century. The best legislative initiative is absence.

  2. Create a fully open, transparent and distributed jury system. All judges and the servants of the law on the ground should be elected directly by the public, rather than officially appointed. In the 21st century, the choice of arbitrators is more important than the election of deputies.

  3. Dramatically increase taxes on all industries associated with the production of raw materials. The country needs to get rid of the Dutch disease, which pulls the country into the abyss for decades. The excess material in the 21st century is a satellite of stagnation.

  4. Eliminate taxes and restrictions on everything connected with the informational sphere. Russia must become the first major global information center that will attract the most progressive and talented people in the world. This is a century of free information and we must embrace it.

  5. Exempt the population from taxes, which ultimately always pays the consumer. We have a duty not only to raise the level of affluence, but also to reduce the conditions that undermine the chances of domestic business to succeed in global competition in a global market.

  6. Provide the regions of Russia with fully autonomous organizations, with small uninhabited areas which will be leased for 100 years to create a system of mini-states. The output of hundreds of projects are effective and free to taxpayers. The 21st century is a century of decentralization and networking.

  7. Allow the free circulation of gold and any electronic currency 100% backed by gold. Russia has become fertile ground for free and reliable means of payment. The national currency is anachronistic; it is a tool of the plunder for the population, and inflation. The 21st century is a century of free non-state currency.

  8. A de-standardized education system. Today’s schools were created in the industrial age and resemble factories, which are imparted to the conveyor belt mentality. Specialists of the 21st century can be prepared only in non-standard educational institutions. The 21st century is a century of unique schools and unique specialists.

  9. Allow taxpayers the right to choose direct cost projects, which are funded by their taxes. Projects can be at any level – from a playground in the neighborhood to a program of colonization of Mars. A party may advise the taxpayer, but not decide for him. The 21st century is a century free of exploitative tax.

  10. End the registration, a passport as a separate entity, visas, conscription, and other vestiges of feudalism. Attempts to restrict the right of movement and recruit young people to Russian Armed Forces is a slavery that leads to an outflow of the best minds to other countries. The 21st century is a century without feudal boundaries.

My views are that these sound like good suggestions.

The country needs to get rid of the Dutch disease, which pulls the country into the abyss for decades. The excess material in the 21st century is a satellite of stagnation.

We have a duty not only to raise the level of affluence

Wut?

Other than that it looks good. Hasn't a hope in hell of happening though.
